lesson_title: Delta, Dials and the Ghost Root: Algebra, Functions and Trig Essentials
hook_text: The algebra says x = 1. The equation says NO. Meet the ghost root.
clip_script: And the surd equation carries a sting. Root of x plus three equals x minus three. Square both sides: x plus three equals x squared minus six x plus nine, so x squared minus seven x plus six equals zero — x equals six or x equals one. Now the compulsory check: x equals six gives root nine, three, and six minus three, three — valid. X equals one gives root four, two, but one minus three is minus two — invalid. Squaring manufactures ghost solutions, and the check is not politeness; it is part of the method.
visual_style: Two candidate answers walk toward the original equation like a border checkpoint; x equals six shows matching stamps, three and three, and passes; x equals one flashes two versus minus two, turns translucent and dissolves — a ghost caught at the gate.
mood: Ghost-story reveal — the answer that algebra invented and the original equation refuses.
pacing: Brisk squaring and factorising, slow-down at the checkpoint, sharp dissolve on the ghost, confident close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and send every ghost root home before the marker meets it.
